description_full: Magnera Corporation manufactures and sells non-woven and related products worldwide. It sells its products primarily into consumer-oriented end markets, such as healthcare, and personal care. The company offers personal care and consumer solution products and components of products including medical garments, wipes, dryer sheets, filtration, baby diapers and adult incontinence. The company also offers tea bags, coffee filters, wipes, cable wrap, filtration, baby diapers and adult incontinence. The company is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina.

Each employee generates $4K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $2K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 6× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: Magnera Corporation is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $442M market cap on $3.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +43% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 0% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 13% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $36M in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 7.8× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
